title: PoE 2 Respec: Reset Passives, Weapon Sets and Ascendancy
summary: How to refund normal passives, Weapon Set passives, and reset your Ascendancy in PoE 2: the NPC or screen, prerequisites, risk, whether a Trial is required, and the gold cost.
description: A decision-first PoE 2 respec guide: a refund boundary matrix for normal passives, Weapon Set passives, Ascendancy resets, and Atlas passive choices; weapon-set pairing rules; how to clear and re-pick an Ascendancy at the right Trial or Altar; gold cost breakdown; and a before-respec checklist.
prerequisites: You have passive, Weapon Set, or Ascendancy points you want to change
You understand that refunds cost gold and some resets require redoing a Trial
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: PoE 2 passive skill tree and Ascendancy panel, the screens where refunds and resets happen

items.title: How do I refund normal passives?
body: Open the passive screen and unallocate points for gold; the cost scales with how many points you refund and your character level.
You do not need an NPC or a Trial for ordinary passive refunds.

items.title: How do I reset my Ascendancy?
body: Clearing the relevant Trial or Altar resets your allocated Ascendancy points so you can re-pick the class and nodes.
This is higher risk: you lose all current Ascendancy points until you re-earn them by completing the Trial again.

items.title: Why are Weapon Set refunds paired?
body: Weapon Sets allocate passives per set, and when both sets are linked the refund must be handled as a pair.
Refund the linked sets together, or you may strand points you intended to keep.

sections.title: Refund boundary matrix
sections.intro: What you can refund, where, what it costs, and whether a Trial is required. Verify NPC names and Trial requirements against the current client before acting.

rows.prerequisite: Points are allocated; gold on hand
rows.risk: Low - reversible, but gold cost grows with points refunded and character level
rows.cost: Gold, scales with points and level

rows.prerequisite: Both Weapon Sets allocated; refund handled per set or as a pair
rows.risk: Medium - paired sets can strand points if refunded incorrectly

rows.prerequisite: Must clear the Trial/Altar again to re-pick class and nodes
rows.risk: High - all Ascendancy points lost until re-earned
rows.cost: Trial completion plus any associated costs

rows.prerequisite: Atlas points allocated; some Master choices lock once committed
rows.risk: Medium - committed Master choices may not be freely reversible

sections.title: Before you change anything
paragraphs: Respecs are cheap to start and expensive to finish. Confirm what you actually need to change before spending gold or a Trial.
bullets: Open a build planner and map the target tree so you only move the points you must.
Check gold on hand; large refunds can cost far more than a few points.
For Ascendancy changes, confirm which Trial or Altar is current for that class before committing.
Save or screenshot your current setup so you can revert if the new plan feels worse.

sections.title: Normal passive refunds
paragraphs: Ordinary passive points are the most flexible. You refund them directly in the passive screen for gold, with no NPC errand and no Trial.
bullets: Cost scales with the number of points refunded and your character level, so prune in batches you actually need.
You can refund a single point or the whole tree; the price difference is purely the count.
Refunded points return to the pool immediately and can be reallocated the same session.
If a node is required by a cluster you want to keep, refund from the outer edge inward to avoid stranding pathing.

sections.title: Weapon Set passive refunds
paragraphs: Weapon Sets let you allocate passives per set. When both sets are linked, the refund must respect that pairing or you can strand points.
bullets: Refund the linked sets together rather than one side at a time.
If a set shares pathing with the other, removing it may also affect the paired set's reach.
Re-plan both sets on a planner before refunding so the paired layout stays valid.
Treat Weapon Set refunds as a paired operation, not two independent ones.

sections.title: Ascendancy reset
paragraphs: Changing your Ascendancy class or reworking its nodes is the highest-risk respec. Clearing the relevant Trial or Altar resets allocated Ascendancy points so you can re-pick.
bullets: You lose all current Ascendancy points until you re-earn them by completing the Trial or reaching the Altar again.
Confirm the current Trial or Altar requirement for your class, because requirements shift between patches.
Plan the new Ascendancy path before resetting so you do not sit on zero points.
A full Ascendancy change is worth it only when the new class clearly beats your current one for the content you run.

sections.title: Cost breakdown
sections.intro: Respec cost is mostly gold for passives and time/Trial for Ascendancy. Scale expectations before you commit.

rows.detail: A small number of points costs little; good for minor fixes.

rows.item: Refund many points or full tree
rows.detail: Cost rises with points refunded and character level; batch only what you need.
Paired sets may require refunding both, doubling the touched-point count.
No direct gold, but you must re-clear the Trial or Altar and re-earn every point.

sections.note: Gold cost for passives scales with count and level; Ascendancy cost is the Trial run itself. Verify exact scaling in the current client.

sections.title: Small change vs full rebuild
paragraphs: Match the method to the size of the change. Most 'respecs' are tiny and should never touch Ascendancy.
bullets: Small tweak (a few nodes): refund those points only; do not open the Ascendancy screen.
Phase transition (new gear tier): refund the affected pathing and re-path; still gold only.
Full rebuild (different archetype): consider Weapon Set respec and possibly Ascendancy reset together.
Only reset Ascendancy when the new class clearly outperforms for your content; otherwise a passive reshuffle suffices.

steps.label: Save current config
body: Screenshot or export your passive, Weapon Set, and Ascendancy setup.
Keep the old plan in case the new one feels worse.

steps.label: Plan the target
body: Use a build planner to map the exact target tree and Ascendancy.
Confirm which points actually move so you refund the minimum.

steps.label: Check gold and Trial
body: Confirm gold on hand covers the passive refund count.
For Ascendancy, confirm the current Trial or Altar requirement before committing.

steps.label: Handle paired sets
body: If Weapon Sets are linked, plan both sets together.
Refund the pair as one operation to avoid stranding points.

sections.title: Community questions
sections.intro: Common respec questions from Reddit and video comments, with our read and a direct suggestion.

cards.title: Refund cost exploded
body: Problem: refunding the whole tree cost far more than expected.
Evidence: gold cost scales with points refunded and character level.
Suggestion: refund only the points you must; batch minimally.

cards.title: Ascendancy reset lost everything
body: Problem: resetting cleared all Ascendancy points at once.
Evidence: a reset returns all points until you re-earn them via the Trial.
Suggestion: plan the new path first; only reset when the new class clearly wins.

cards.title: Weapon Set stranded points
body: Problem: refunding one set broke the other's pathing.
Evidence: linked sets must be refunded as a pair.
Suggestion: plan and refund both sets together.

cards.title: Trial requirement changed
body: Problem: the old Trial path no longer works for the class.
Evidence: Trial/Altar requirements shift between patches.
Suggestion: confirm the current requirement in the client before resetting.

entries.takeaway: Refund passives in batches, handle Weapon Sets as pairs, and only reset Ascendancy when the new class clearly beats your current one.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Most respec confusion is about cost scaling or paired sets, not a bug. Read the symptom, then check the matrix.
bullets: Cost too high: refund only the points you must; gold scales with count and level.
Weapon Set broke: you refunded one side of a linked pair; re-plan and refund both.
Ascendancy empty: a reset returns all points until re-earned via the Trial.
Trial missing: confirm the current Trial or Altar requirement, which shifts between patches.
Suspected bug: capture your allocated points, gold, and the Trial state before reporting.
